title: PHP2Shell was being exploited before the patch, Chinese hackers used AI agents to break into companies through ConnectWise, and big US banks are blocking agents that use customers’ passwords. 1Password lets agents sign in without seeing passwords, Claude goes auto by default, Uber gives ChatGPT Work to 30,000 staff, OpenAI’s Decisions API and the full Claude Platform on Google Cloud are generally available, Canva launched its own image model, Arc is shutting down, and GitHub applies Copilot’s default policy.
summary: On 22 October 2026: Amazon said attackers tried PHP2Shell four days before the patch and are now trying it widely. Microsoft and TechCrunch detailed how Storm-0940 used the ARTEX AI agent framework and stolen ConnectWise app credentials to try to sign in to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants. Axios reported that Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are blocking or restricting third-party AI agents. 1Password launched 1Password for Agents, and Anthropic said Claude apps will run in auto mode by default from next week. Uber rolled ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 employees. OpenAI made the Decisions API generally available at $0.10 per million input tokens, and Anthropic made the full Claude Platform available on Google Cloud, paid from Google commitments. Canva launched Craft, Arc will stop working on 22 December, and GitHub began applying Copilot’s default policy to unconfigured features.
uncertainty: Amazon reports exploit attempts, not confirmed break-ins, and the PHP Foundation says it knows of no successful remote code execution. TechCrunch’s ‘almost 3,000 sign-ins per minute’ refers to a separate Storm-0940 password-spray peak that Microsoft says produced no successful logins; Microsoft says a successful sign-in does not necessarily mean data was taken. The bank story rests on Axios’s unnamed sources, and Morgan Stanley says it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms. Anthropic’s auto mode safety data comes from Claude Code testing, not the other apps. Customer speed and cost figures for the Decisions API and Canva’s quality claims are the companies’ own. Uber has not disclosed costs.

stories.theme: PHP2Shell was being tried by attackers days before the patch. Check, don’t just update
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Amazon said its threat intelligence team saw an attempt to exploit PHP2Shell, the two critical PHP flaws patched on 21 October, on 17 October, four days before the fix, against one of its MadPot decoy servers and from an IP address on an anonymising network. Amazon says several working exploit demonstrations appeared from about 02:00 UTC on 21 October, before the embargo lifted at 14:00 UTC, and that it is now seeing broad exploitation attempts in the wild. The PHP Foundation says details of the bugs leaked before it could release the fix; its executive director, Elizabeth Barron, told The Verge that to its knowledge no attempt at remote code execution has succeeded, but that updating is imperative. Amazon says there is no configuration-only workaround, and advises upgrading, considering blocking multipart file uploads where they are not needed, and searching logs for unusual POST requests carrying PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS.
stories.matters: Yesterday’s advice was to patch fast. Now the question is also whether a server was probed before you patched. A clean update does not prove nothing happened in the days before it.
stories.imply: Treat the public disclosure date as the latest possible start of attacks, not the earliest. Incident checks need to look back before the patch date.
uses: Confirm every PHP site and product is on 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, including ones run by agencies and hosts.
Ask IT or your host to search web logs from 17 October onwards for POST requests carrying PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS.
Block multipart file uploads on sites that do not need them, as Amazon suggests.
stories.example: An e-commerce team that patched on 21 October asks its host to check logs back to 17 October. Two odd upload requests turn up on a staging site, which is rebuilt and its keys rotated.
stories.audience: IT and security teams, website owners and the agencies and hosts that run PHP sites.
stories.watch: Confirmed break-ins, as opposed to attempts. How the exploit details leaked. Fixes for products that bundle PHP.

source.title: The Verge: The disastrous PHP vulnerabilities were exploited days before the patch, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Hackers attempted to exploit the PHP flaws impacting sites across the web days before they were patched, according to a report from Amazon Threat Intelligence.

stories.theme: Chinese hackers used an AI agent framework to break into companies through ConnectWise backup
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 TechCrunch reported that China state-aligned hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching ConnectWise’s cloud backup service, formerly SkyKick. In a report published on 21 October, Microsoft says the group, Storm-0940, stole the credentials of ConnectWise’s trusted app, which customers had already granted access to their Microsoft 365 data, and used them to try to sign in to more than 2,250 customer tenants without any user signing in. It ran the attacks with ARTEX, an open-source penetration testing framework in which AI agents carry out an attack from reconnaissance to data theft with little human help. Microsoft says it saw cases where the time from first targeting to privileged access was under three hours, and agents changing app credentials and privileges that can act as a backdoor after the original app is fixed. ConnectWise paused access to its cloud backup service; as of Thursday it said it was working on restoring it.
stories.matters: Apps you have already approved, like backup tools, can reach your email and files without anyone logging in. When attackers use AI agents, the time from break-in to damage shrinks to hours.
stories.imply: Third-party app access in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace needs the same scrutiny as staff accounts. Alerts that wait for the next working day are too slow.
uses: If you use ConnectWise Cloud Backup, follow its containment guidance and check the app’s sign-ins and changes since early October.
Ask IT to review service principal sign-ins and any new app credentials, owners or privileged roles in Microsoft 365.
List the third-party apps with access to company mail and files, and remove the ones no one uses.
stories.example: An IT manager finds an unused backup app still has read access to every mailbox. She removes it, then sets an alert for any new credentials added to apps.
stories.audience: IT and security teams, managed service providers and companies on Microsoft 365.
stories.watch: How many tenants had data taken. ConnectWise’s restoration timeline. Whether ARTEX shows up in more attacks.

source.title: TechCrunch: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise, 22 October 2026
source.quote: By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files.

stories.theme: Big US banks are blocking AI agents that log in with customers’ passwords
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Axios reported that major US banks are detecting unauthorised third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, some trying to take actions that appear independent of what the user asked. These are usually agents a customer has handed their login to, which goes against most banks’ rules that people log in themselves. According to Axios’s sources, Morgan Stanley has begun blocking third-party agents, and JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are also restricting them. Most banks have allowed, or are moving towards, read-only access, so agents can see financial information but not act. A Chase spokesperson said customers should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone, and sources said many banks cannot tell whether agent activity was directed by the user.
stories.matters: Agents that pay bills, move money or file expenses on someone’s behalf may suddenly be locked out. Sharing a bank password with an agent can also break the bank’s terms.
stories.imply: Banks are moving agents to read-only, official access. Finance workflows built on agents with shared logins need a different route.
uses: Check whether any finance or expense workflow lets an agent log in to a bank account with a person’s password, and stop it.
Ask your bank which agent or API access it supports, and whether it is read-only.
Tell staff not to give bank logins to personal AI assistants.
stories.example: A small business owner’s assistant agent had been logging in to the business bank account to download statements. She switches it to the bank’s read-only data feed instead.
stories.audience: Finance teams, small business owners and anyone using AI agents with bank accounts.
stories.watch: Formal agent access rules from banks. Whether regulators weigh in. More blocks beyond the four named banks.

source.title: Axios: Scoop: Unvetted AI agents are accessing U.S. bank accounts, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, with some agents attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources tell Axios.

stories.theme: 1Password lets AI agents sign in for you without ever seeing the password
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 1Password announced 1Password for Agents. When an agent reaches a sign-in page, it asks for a credential from your vault; you review and approve the request in 1Password, and 1Password fills the login into the site directly, so the agent never sees the password or one-time code. Integrations with Meta’s Muse and SpaceXSI’s Grok Bot are rolling out over the coming days; Anthropic’s Claude Duet, OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work and dots, and Town’s Townie are coming soon; and integrations with Instinct, Browserbase, Browser Use, Dana, KERNEL, Perplexity, Ramp, Tomo and Wajo are planned. It is available at no extra cost for 1Password Individual and Family accounts on 1Password.com.
stories.matters: Giving an agent your password, or pasting it into a prompt, hands over access beyond the task. Approving each login keeps a person in charge of what the agent can reach.
stories.imply: Agent sign-in is becoming a separate, approvable step. Expect password managers and identity tools to become the gate for agent access.
uses: If you use 1Password at home, try it with one agent on a low-risk site before using it for work accounts.
Ask your 1Password business admin when 1Password for Agents is coming to company accounts.
Stop pasting passwords into chat prompts, and change any you already have.
stories.example: A freelancer lets her agent book a venue. When it hits the venue’s login page, she approves the request on her phone and 1Password fills it in, without the password going into the chat.
stories.audience: People using personal AI agents, IT and security teams, and 1Password customers.
stories.watch: Business plan availability. When the ChatGPT Work and Claude Duet integrations go live. Whether banks accept this kind of agent sign-in.

source.title: 1Password: Give personal AI agents access without giving them your passwords, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Now, with 1Password for Agents, your agent can request to use a credential from your vault, and if you approve the request, 1Password directly auto-fills the credentials in the destination site so the agent doesn’t have access to the credentials.

stories.theme: From next week, Claude will stop asking you to approve each step
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Anthropic said auto mode will become the default for new sessions in most Claude apps on Pro, Max and Team plans from next week. Instead of asking you to approve each action, an automated check reviews them: safe actions go ahead, and risky ones are blocked while Claude looks for another route. You can switch back to manual at any time. Enterprise admins will get an email before auto mode becomes the default for their organisations. Auto mode has been the default in Claude Code since 14 August; Anthropic says it routes each action through a classifier aimed at blocking actions that are irreversible, destructive or aimed outside your environment, and that in its Claude Code testing it matched or beat manual review on every measure, partly because users approve 97% of permission prompts.
stories.matters: Claude will do more on its own in the apps people use at work, including actions in connected tools. Fewer prompts means faster work, but also fewer moments where a person stops a mistake.
stories.imply: Agents are moving from approve-every-step to automated checks. Teams need to decide which actions still require a person.
uses: Team admins: check before next week whether you want auto mode on, and tell staff how to switch back to manual.
Enterprise admins: watch for Anthropic’s email and decide your default before it changes.
Keep human approval for sending, paying and deleting in connected apps, and test what auto mode blocks.
stories.example: A team lead tries auto mode on a low-risk research task, sees Claude complete several connected-app steps without prompts, then keeps manual mode for the shared finance workspace.
stories.audience: Claude Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise users and admins.
stories.watch: The exact rollout date. Which actions the check blocks outside code. Admin controls for Team plans.

source.title: Claude by Anthropic: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team plans (updated 22 October 2026)
source.quote: Enterprise admins will get an email before auto mode becomes the default for their organizations.

stories.theme: Uber gives ChatGPT Work to all 30,000 employees, then will measure what they do with it
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Uber and OpenAI said ChatGPT Work, the agent inside ChatGPT Enterprise, is rolling out to Uber’s whole global workforce of more than 30,000 people. It connects to Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar and Slack, and GPT-6.1 Sol is the default model. Uber piloted it with 1,000 employees earlier this year; about 80% were not engineers, Uber’s VP of engineering, Sumanth Sukumar, told TechCrunch, and they used it to analyse operations data, localise training materials and build personal dashboards. The rollout comes with an internal AI skills library, approved integrations and training. Uber did not say what it is spending, and has not settled how staff will use it: it will track usage and workflows and use the results to guide how it deploys AI.
stories.matters: This is a company-wide agent rollout aimed mostly at non-engineers. The plan is to give everyone access with guardrails, then measure, rather than pick use cases first.
stories.imply: Agents are becoming standard issue for whole workforces. The work shifts to training, shared skills and measuring results.
uses: Start a shared library of prompts and skills that work for your team, as Uber has.
Pair a technical person with a team for two weeks to automate part of their job, like Uber’s ‘AI pods’.
Decide upfront what you will measure, such as hours saved or workflows built.
stories.example: A finance team gets ChatGPT Work access, connects Drive and Calendar, and keeps a shared list of the prompts that produce good meeting briefs and variance reports.
stories.audience: Operations, finance, HR and IT leaders planning company-wide AI rollouts.
stories.watch: What Uber reports from its usage tracking. Cost. Whether other large employers follow.

source.title: TechCrunch: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,

stories.theme: OpenAI’s Decisions API is generally available: fast yes/no and pick-one answers for apps and agents
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available. Built with GPT-6 Luna, it answers questions with bounded answers, such as yes/no, pick-one or a score, from text, images and structured data, up to 10 times faster than asking GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. Since the beta, OpenAI has added a GPT-Live integration so voice apps can react as people speak, prompt caching, native JSON inputs, processing in the US and EU, and up to 400 questions per request. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens, $0.01 for cached input, with no charge for output. OpenAI quotes customers including Box, Datadog, Ramp, Sierra and Speak on speed and cost gains. TechCrunch notes it competes with TypeSafe’s Jev.
stories.matters: Many agent steps are small decisions: which team handles this ticket, is this a refund, is this safe to send. A cheap, fast model for those can cut cost and waiting time.
stories.imply: Expect apps to split work: small decision models for routing and checks, larger models for writing. Price per decision is now a cost line to compare.
uses: Use it to route support tickets or forms to the right team instead of a full chat model call.
Ask your developers to test whether checks such as ‘does this need approval?’ get cheaper or faster.
Compare cost per decision against your current model, using OpenAI’s input-only pricing.
stories.example: A support team sends each incoming email to the Decisions API with three questions: refund or not, which product, how urgent. It routes tickets in well under a second.
stories.audience: Developers and product teams building apps, agents and voice tools.
stories.watch: Real-world accuracy against larger models. TypeSafe’s response. Rival decision models from others.

source.title: OpenAI: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Decisions API costs $0.10 per million input tokens.

stories.theme: The full Claude Platform comes to Google Cloud, paid from your Google commitment
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Anthropic made Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) generally available. Google Cloud customers get the full Claude Platform, including managed agents (beta), code execution, computer use, agent skills, the Files API, web search and prompt caching, with new features and betas arriving the same day as on Anthropic’s own platform. It uses Google Cloud IAM credentials, is billed on a single Google Cloud invoice, and draws down existing Google Cloud commitments. It runs on US and Global endpoints, and Anthropic acts as data processor; the existing Google-managed option, where Google is the data processor, remains. Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are available, and Fast mode for Opus 5.5, up to 2.5 times faster output, is generally available at $8 and $40 per million input and output tokens.
stories.matters: Companies on Google Cloud can use Claude’s newest features without a separate contract, and pay from money already committed to Google. The day before, OpenAI announced its models are coming to Google Cloud too.
stories.imply: Your cloud commitment is becoming a budget for any frontier model. Buyers get leverage, but must choose who processes their data.
uses: If you have a Google Cloud commitment, ask your account team how Claude usage will count against it.
Have legal check which option you need: Anthropic as data processor, or Google-managed with Google as processor.
Price Fast mode only for interactive work where speed matters, at $8 and $40 per million tokens.
stories.example: A software company that builds on Claude moves its agent to the Anthropic-managed Google Cloud offering, keeps prompt caching, and counts the spend against its existing Google commitment.
stories.audience: CTOs, finance and procurement teams, and developers on Google Cloud.
stories.watch: Regional endpoints beyond the US and Global. Whether pricing differs from Anthropic direct. A similar move on other clouds.

source.title: Claude by Anthropic: The full Claude Platform, available on Google Cloud, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Billing is through a single Google Cloud invoice and Claude usage draws down your existing Google Cloud commitment.

stories.theme: Canva launches Craft, its own image model trained on designs rather than photos
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 Canva released Canva Craft, its first image generation model. It works in two stages: it first plans the layout, including how elements relate, their relative size and the text to render, then generates an image of up to 2K resolution in any of 30 aspect ratios. Canva says it was trained on human-designed templates from its library, such as posters, social posts, presentations, menus and text-heavy layouts, rather than photographs, and that images can be turned into layered, editable designs. It is available to all Canva users from the Dream Lab tab and through the Canva API, and Canva plans to bring it to ChatGPT and Gemini through its MCP connector. Cheaper versions, Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, are coming.
stories.matters: Marketing and comms teams already in Canva get an image model built for layouts and legible text, which general image models often get wrong. Results can be edited as designs, not just regenerated.
stories.imply: Design tools are building their own models instead of renting them. Expect quicker on-brand drafts inside the tools teams already use.
uses: Try Craft in Dream Lab on a poster or social post with real text, and check the spelling and layout.
Convert a generated image into a layered design and edit the text instead of regenerating.
Check your brand and licensing rules for AI-generated images before using Craft in campaigns.
stories.example: A comms officer generates an event poster in Dream Lab with the date and venue in the image, converts it into a layered design, and swaps in the brand font.
stories.audience: Marketing, comms and design teams, and anyone using Canva at work.
stories.watch: Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast. The ChatGPT and Gemini integration through MCP. Plan limits and pricing.

source.title: TechCrunch: Canva releases its first image generation model, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab.

stories.theme: Arc browser shuts down on 22 December. Plan the move now
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 The Browser Company said it will shut down its Arc browser on 22 December 2026 and is pointing users to Dia, its AI-first browser, citing the rising cost of keeping a browser secure in the age of AI. New Arc accounts can no longer be created. On 23 November, Arc Search on iOS and Android loses its AI features, including Browse for Me, and sign-in and tab sync. On 22 December, Arc stops working entirely on Mac and Windows, accounts are deactivated, and personal data is deleted within 30 days. Passwords, bookmarks, extensions and history transfer to Dia, and Arc features remain free in Dia, with AI optional. The Browser Company was bought by Atlassian in 2025.
stories.matters: Anyone who works in Arc has two months to move bookmarks, passwords and setups before the browser stops and the data is deleted.
stories.imply: AI browsers are replacing older ones, and the security burden is the stated reason. Moving to Dia means deciding whether its AI features are allowed at work.
uses: If your team uses Arc, set a migration date well before 22 December.
Export or transfer passwords and bookmarks, and check that saved logins still work afterwards.
If you move to Dia, check your company’s rules on AI browser features before turning them on.
stories.example: A design studio where half the team uses Arc picks a Friday in November to move everyone to Dia or Chrome, with IT checking passwords and extensions.
stories.audience: Arc users, IT teams supporting Macs and Windows PCs, and startups that standardised on Arc.
stories.watch: Data deletion after 22 December. Dia’s enterprise and security controls. Whether Atlassian bundles Dia with its products.

source.title: TechCrunch: Arc browser sunsets December 22 as The Browser Company doubles down on Dia, 22 October 2026
source.quote: On December 22, Arc will stop working entirely on Mac and Windows.

stories.theme: GitHub starts applying Copilot’s default policy to settings you never configured
stories.changed: On Thursday 22 October 2026 GitHub began gradually enforcing its global default policy for generally available Copilot features on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise, with the rollout running through 26 October, so it may take effect at different times for different enterprises and organisations. Once it applies, eligible features, client capabilities and MCP servers left unconfigured are set to the chosen global default: Enabled, Disabled, or Let organisations decide. GitHub says this is a one-time change; later changes to the default will not change settings already in place. Features you have explicitly enabled or disabled keep that setting, and preview features stay opt-in. The setting is under AI Controls → Copilot → Default policy for new features.
stories.matters: Copilot features and MCP servers nobody chose may switch on or off across your organisation this week. If your default is Enabled, new AI capabilities can reach developers without a review.
stories.imply: AI admin settings now default to on unless someone decides otherwise. ‘Unconfigured’ is becoming a choice in itself.
uses: Copilot admins: check AI Controls → Copilot → Default policy for new features before 26 October.
Set explicit choices for MCP servers and features you want reviewed first.
Tell developers which Copilot features to expect, so changes are not a surprise.
stories.example: An enterprise admin finds the default set to Enabled, switches it to Let organisations decide, and explicitly disables two MCP servers until security reviews them.
stories.audience: GitHub enterprise and organisation admins, engineering managers and security teams.
stories.watch: Which features count as eligible. Admin feedback on the rollout. Similar defaults in other AI tools.

source.title: GitHub Changelog: Global default for Copilot features generally available, 22 October 2026
source.quote: Explicit choices are preserved. If you’ve enabled or disabled an individual feature, the rollout won’t change that setting.
